turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, yeah, nice to meet you too. So, the main thing that finally pushed me to come in is work. I’m an insurance claims clerk, and I just keep getting up from my workstation during the day. Even when I know I’m supposed to stay put and finish my claim reviews, I’m always wandering off. 

It doesn't really help that my desk is right by the breakroom, honestly. They just got this new coffee machine in there—one of those fancy ones that grinds the beans right in front of you? It’s so loud, but the coffee is actually pretty good. Much better than the stuff we had when I was in college. I only went for a couple of years, but man, the dining hall coffee was basically just brown water. I swear they watered it down to save money, or maybe the machine was just broken. I used to complain to the cafeteria manager, but he never did anything about it. 

But, um, yeah... I just can't seem to stay in my seat to get my claims done.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes being distracted by extraneous stimuli, specifically the loud new coffee machine in the nearby breakroom, which also derails their train of thought during the conversation.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient explicitly states they keep getting up from their workstation and wandering off, even though they know they are supposed to stay seated to finish their work.

turns.doctor_question: Did you have this same kind of trouble staying seated and on task when you were a child?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, looking back, I guess this isn't really a brand new thing for me. Like, in elementary school, my teachers used to always write on my report cards that I was a bright kid, but I was constantly losing my worksheets. I used to keep them in this one folder, it was a Transformers folder. The holographic kind where the picture changes when you tilt it? I loved that thing. I got it at the school book fair. Man, book fairs were the absolute best back then. They always had those cool erasers shaped like aliens, and those little pointers with the hands on the end. I think I bought a poster of a Lamborghini once, too, which I hung up in my room until the tape ruined the paint and my mom got so mad. 

But, um, wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, school. Yeah, so my teachers said I missed instructions a lot and they always had to come over and remind me to actually finish my classwork.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient confirms the doctor's question about having trouble staying on task as a child by answering 'Yeah.'
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient explicitly states that they missed instructions and needed reminders to finish their classwork.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient reports that in elementary school they were constantly losing their worksheets.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility during the response by going off on a tangent about a folder and book fair, temporarily losing their train of thought.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient confirms the doctor's question about having trouble staying seated as a child by answering 'Yeah.'

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually energetic or euphoric for several days in a row?
turns.patient_response:
Unusually energetic? Um, no, not really. I mean, I wish I had that kind of energy, honestly. The only time I get really wired is if I drink too many of those Celsius drinks. Have you tried those? The sparkling peach one is really good. I actually bought a whole case of them at Costco last weekend. 

Man, Costco on a Sunday is an absolute nightmare. People just stop their giant carts right in the middle of the aisle to eat a tiny piece of sausage on a toothpick. Like, you're blocking the entire bakery section for a free sample! I ended up buying a giant tub of those peanut butter pretzels I didn't even need just because I was trapped in that aisle and got bored waiting for this one family to move. They're pretty good pretzels, though, I've been snacking on them at my desk. 

But, uh... wait, what were you asking? Like, energetic for days in a row? No, definitely not. I'm usually just regular tired.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates being easily distracted by unrelated thoughts, going on a long tangent about energy drinks and Costco before forgetting the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient explicitly denies experiencing periods of feeling unusually euphoric or energetic.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient explicitly denies having periods of unusual energy lasting for days in a row.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often have intense, unstable relationships where your feelings about someone swing quickly from really positive to really negative?
turns.patient_response:
Um, unstable relationships? No, not really. I mean, I have my girlfriend, Sarah. We've been together for like three years now. She's great, honestly. We met at this trivia night at a pub near my old apartment. I used to go every Tuesday with my buddy Mark. Mark is the kind of guy who knows the most useless facts, like he can name all the U.S. presidents in order, backwards. It's wild. But anyway, Sarah was on another team, and they beat us by one point because of a question about the moon landing. 

Speaking of the moon, did you know that the footprints left by the astronauts are probably still there because there's no wind? I watched this whole documentary about it on Netflix the other night. I started it at like 11 PM and next thing I knew it was 2 in the morning and I was reading Wikipedia articles about the Apollo missions instead of sleeping. I do that a lot, actually, just go down these random internet rabbit holes when I should be resting for work. 

But, uh, sorry, what was the question? Relationships? Yeah, no, Sarah and I are pretty solid. No crazy swings or anything like that. We just kind of hang out and watch movies mostly.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by losing track of the doctor's question due to unrelated thoughts, and describes a habit of getting distracted by internet rabbit holes when they should be sleeping.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient talks excessively, providing a long, rambling, and tangential story about a trivia night and the moon landing before finally returning to the original question.

turns.doctor_question: Besides work, does your distractibility cause problems in other parts of your life, like at home or in daily tasks?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, it definitely spills over. I mean, at home I'm always starting things and not finishing them. Like, I'll go to do the laundry, but on the way to the machine I'll see the mail on the counter, so I start opening that. And then there's a bill I need to pay, so I sit down at my laptop, but then I remember I wanted to look up that actor from that movie we watched last night. The guy who was in that one superhero movie? Not Marvel, the other one. DC, right? I always get those mixed up. My buddy Mark is super into comics and he gets so annoyed when I confuse them. He actually went to Comic-Con last year and spent like five hundred dollars on a replica sword. Which is crazy to me, where do you even put a sword in a one-bedroom apartment? 

But anyway, yeah, it's bad at work too, honestly. I'm an insurance claims clerk, and I forget simple work follow-ups more than I want to admit. Like, I'll totally mean to return a claimant's call, or update a diary note on a file, or send out a form I was supposed to email earlier that day, and it just... poof. Gone from my brain until someone asks me about it. It's really frustrating.

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient reports starting chores like laundry at home but failing to finish them.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes being easily distracted by extraneous stimuli like mail and unrelated thoughts about movies and friends.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient admits to frequently forgetting daily work activities, such as returning calls and sending forms.
